macros.name: a
macros.doc: \a. opens a level of sub-examples; \b. through \f. add further items at the level currently open.

macros.name: altg
macros.doc: Glossed alternatives: written in both lines of \exg. (objects, then glosses); both-braced, centred.

macros.name: AltgTransFont
macros.doc: Two settings of its own, redefined with \renewcommand: \AltgColSep (default 1.2em), the gap between the object and gloss stacks, and \AltgTransFont (default \normalfont), the font of the gloss stack.

macros.name: altn
macros.doc: \altn is set in text mode: the alternatives are the rows of a tabular, braced on both sides with drawn braces, so no mathematics is involved (the package needs tikz, not amsmath).

macros.name: ea
macros.doc: \ea opens an example; inside one, it opens the next level down; and \z closes whatever the matching \ea opened.

macros.name: exannot
macros.doc: Structural label, set in a column at \ExAnnotColumn; {〈text〉} on the object line in a gloss.

macros.name: ExAnnotColumn
macros.doc: \ExAnnotColumn is where the column is, measured from the left edge of the text block — so “9cm” means what it says on the page, and does not move when the example does.

macros.name: ExAnnotFont
macros.doc: Font of the annotation (\normalfont).

macros.name: ExAnnotSep
macros.doc: \ExAnnotSep (default 1em) is the least gap between an example and the column; give it no stretch or shrink.

macros.name: ExLBr
macros.doc: The number of a top-level example is bracketed by \ExLBr/\ExRBr, and a footnote example’s by \FnExLBr/\FnExRBr.

macros.name: exp
macros.doc: It is the LaTeX kernel’s math operator as well as langsci-gb4e’s item command, and here the mode decides between them: inside math it is the operator, outside it is the item.

macros.name: ExRBr
macros.doc: The number of a top-level example is bracketed by \ExLBr/\ExRBr, and a footnote example’s by \FnExLBr/\FnExRBr.

macros.name: Extopsep
macros.doc: \Extopsep is the space left above and below.

macros.name: FnExLBr
macros.doc: The number of a top-level example is bracketed by \ExLBr/\ExRBr, and a footnote example’s by \FnExLBr/\FnExRBr.

macros.name: gll
macros.doc: \gll takes an object line and a gloss line, each ended by \\; \glll takes three lines.

macros.name: glll
macros.doc: \gll takes an object line and a gloss line, each ended by \\; \glll takes three lines.

macros.name: GlossSep
macros.doc: The space between columns is the macro \GlossSep, a glue specification (default .5em plus .3em minus .1em), changed with \renewcommand.

macros.name: GlossTierFont
macros.doc: Each tier is set with a one-argument command, declared by \GlossTierFont{〈n〉} {〈command〉}.

macros.name: GlossTransRatio
macros.doc: The share of the measure the grid gets is \GlossTransRatio (default .6), and the gap between the two columns is \GlossTransSep (default 2em).

macros.name: GlossTransSep
macros.doc: The share of the measure the grid gets is \GlossTransRatio (default .6), and the gap between the two columns is \GlossTransSep (default 2em).

macros.name: JdgSep
macros.doc: The distance between mark and text is the length \JdgSep (default 0.15em).

macros.name: mvfrom
macros.doc: \mvfrom[〈options〉]{〈label〉}{〈text〉} marks the base position and \mvto[〈options〉] {〈label〉}{〈text〉} the landing site; the 〈text〉 is typeset as it is, so a copy can be greyed out with \textcolor as usual.

macros.name: mvto
macros.doc: \mvfrom[〈options〉]{〈label〉}{〈text〉} marks the base position and \mvto[〈options〉] {〈label〉}{〈text〉} the landing site; the 〈text〉 is typeset as it is, so a copy can be greyed out with \textcolor as usual.

macros.name: rangedash
macros.doc: The range dash is the macro \rangedash (default an en-dash).

macros.name: refrange
macros.doc: \refrange{〈first〉}{〈last〉} sets a compact range over sub-examples, printing “(3a–c)” rather than “(3a)–(3c)”.

macros.name: Refrange
macros.doc: \Refrange sets a range over two whole examples, as (10)–(12).

macros.name: resetExdefaults
macros.doc: \resetExdefaults restores every layout parameter to the values of the mode in force; it is what the package runs for you as it loads.

macros.name: secondrefdash
macros.doc: \rangedash (default --) separates the two ends of a range; \firstrefdash sits between an example number and a sub-example letter in a reference such as “(3a)”, and \secondrefdash between the letter and a roman numeral in “(3a-i)”.

macros.name: SetAltSpoken
macros.doc: The word spoken between stacked alternatives, for \altn and \altg alike: \SetAltSpoken{〈ou〉} gives “aa, bb ou cc”.

macros.name: SetAnnotSpoken
macros.doc: \SetAnnotSpoken{〈text〉} {〈phrase〉} registers a spoken form for a label used throughout (section 7.5).

macros.name: z
macros.doc: \z. pops exactly one level, counting the surrounding prose as the outermost level.
